subject: Ledger cascade: partner credit ingest misbucket — AR / VAT tagging mismatch
messages:
From: Rajesh Gupta <r.gupta@cloudwave.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: billing@cloudwave.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Credit 3321 applied to wrong entity — initial report

Hi Mina / Redwood finance,

Quick heads up — our AR system (partner billing engine) shows that credit note #3321 was applied during your post-bill ingestion to RedWorks Tech LLC invoices instead of Redwood Inference Inc. The credit itself is VAT-tagged for UK reverse-charge and we can see the netting happened against an invoice that is already recognized in a prior period.

Attached: cloudwave_credit_3321.pdf and the raw remit export for 2026-07-13.

Can your team confirm whether the credit was ingested with the wrong legal_entity_id? If so we'll reissue. We understand this can cause AR aging to look overstated for one entity and under-applied for the other, and might cascade into RevRec mapping differences.

I can jump on a quick call if helpful.

—Rajesh
Billing Ops | CloudWave

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
To: Rajesh Gupta <r.gupta@cloudwave.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Credit 3321 applied to wrong entity — initial report

Rajesh — thanks for the note and attachments.

We pulled the ingest logs and see a partner_credit record with entity tag "RW-T" which maps to RedWorks Tech LLC in our old entity table; the credit should have been tagged RW-INF (Redwood Inference Inc). Looks like a lookup fallback triggered during the nightly ETL that handles legacy partner IDs.

Immediate asks:
- Grace, can you assess the GL / RevRec impact if we move the credit from RW-T -> RW-INF? We need a draft JV for the correction and a short memo for audit (SOC2 evidence).
- Karthik, can you open an AR ticket to move the applied amount and reallocate VAT tagging for the invoices in question (see invoice refs in remit export)?
- Rajesh, please hold on reissuing until we confirm whether a journal correction suffices — if not we may need CloudWave to void/reissue.

I'll prepare a scoped rollback plan for the ingest mapping and a temporary hotfix to prevent the fallback for the next two processing windows.

Thanks — Mina
Senior Manager, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Credit 3321 applied to wrong entity — initial report

Mina / Karthik — reviewed the remittance and credit PDF. Preliminary impact:
- Net credit amount: GBP 24,500 (VAT reverse-charge flagged).
- Invoices incorrectly offset (3 invoices) were recognized in prior month close (Jun 2026). If we rebucket the credit to the correct legal entity, revenue recognized for RedWorks Tech LLC will need a contra-revenue entry and Redwood Inference Inc will need the corresponding reduction to AR + adjustment to deferred revenue where applicable.

Proposed accounting correction (draft JV lines):
1) Debit: AR RedWorks Tech LLC GBP 24,500 (to remove the incorrect offset)
2) Credit: AR Redwood Inference Inc GBP 24,500 (to apply credit to correct entity)
3) Debit/Credit: VAT reverse-charge clearing as appropriate (we'll net to zero given reverse-charge nature once entity is corrected)

Notes:
- We should run a mini-close impact report to surface any revenue recognition differences across JP legs; I estimate impact to recognized revenue this quarter could be GBP 24.5k but may be split by entity.
- Need sign-off from legal on cross-entity movement (intercompany settlement) — tagging Karthik for operational coordination and Rajesh for the external side.

I'll draft the memo and upload to Drive.

—Grace
Director, Accounting Operations

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: rajesh.gupta@cloudwave.com, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Credit 3321 applied to wrong entity — action plan and ticket

Rajesh / team — opened AR ticket AR-7891 (link in related_links) to trace the applied allocations and queue the reallocation. Action plan summary:
1) Freeze any automated re-reconciliations for partner CloudWave until 2026-07-16 23:59 PT.
2) Run targeted reapply job to move the application from entity RW-T -> RW-INF on the invoice ids in remit_export_20260713.csv.
3) If reapply fails due to accounting close locks, we'll perform GL JVs (Grace draft) and a documentation trail for audit.
4) CloudWave to confirm if they prefer a reissue credit (void + new credit) instead of our JV approach.

Please confirm by EOD PT and share any constraints (tax/legal) on your side, Rajesh.

Attachment: quick mapping CSV exported from our ingest (snippet).

—Karthik
Revenue Ops

From: Rajesh Gupta <r.gupta@cloudwave.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Credit 3321 applied to wrong entity — action plan and ticket

Thanks everyone — CloudWave will hold reissue. We ran an internal check: the partner export shows legacy_legal_id=RW-T which matches the lookup anomaly Karthik noted. We are comfortable with Redwood doing the reapply or GL JV; preference is reapply to keep our AR history intact.

I'll provide a signed attestation and the remittance verification file by EOD. Expect inbound: remit_export_20260713.csv (attached) and an email from our tax team if any further VAT evidence is required.

If you need anything signed for intercompany movement, loop in our finance controller and I'll expedite.

—Rajesh
Billing Ops | CloudWave
